answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can endorse another identity; endorsements mature only after a delay, and a random audit can slash the endorsers if linked accounts share control or recycle funds. This makes a raven-like burst of fresh identities useless until real capital is locked and trusted peers accept risk. A vine of colluding accounts also exposes its sponsors to compounding losses, while velvet-smooth fake profiles still cost the attacker capital, time, and reachable endorsers.
